utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Okay, um, I think maybe we can start? Is everyone here?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Everyone but Jamal. He's out till Monday.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Right, right. So, uh, first thing, the intranet banner for the benefits webinar.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Oh, I saw that. Bao sent me the draft yesterday and it still had last year's date on it.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Did he, okay. Can you, um, can you ping him?

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Sure. It's the kind of thing where you stare at it for ten minutes and then still miss it, you know?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Just fix the date.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, I'll tell him.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Is the webinar still the twelfth or did that move?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: I think maybe the twelfth? Jonas, you had the invite list.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Twelfth, ten o'clock. Forty-one people registered as of this morning, so about half of who we invited.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: That's not bad for a Thursday.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: It's a Thursday, yeah. Last year we got maybe thirty.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Good. Good. So, uh, the other thing, the review thing. The, um, the performance review question.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Oh, finally.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Well, Thandi asked me last week what we're even planning for the cycle, and I, I didn't have a clean answer.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Planning for which cycle? We only have the one.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Right, that's, that's sort of the point. Where we stand is the December one.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: The one with the self-assessment forms due the first week of December.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Yes. That one. And I just want to hear where everyone is on it before I take anything back.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Okay so, I mean, wait, can I - sorry, were we talking about the form template too?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Not today, no.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Okay. Okay, then. So my view is we just keep it. One review, December, the whole company, same as we've always done it.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Keep it as is, no changes at all?

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Pretty much, yeah.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Why, though? Honestly a lot of people complain they hear nothing for eleven months.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: They do, I know, I hear it too.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Hear it from who?

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Mostly the newer folks. But it's not -

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: I'm only saying, if I'm a new hire, December is a long way off.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Sure. But look at what it costs. A manager sits down and, I mean, it's about six hours for each report by the time they've written it up.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Six hours is the number from the survey?

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Roughly, yeah, it was five to seven depending on the manager. And then on our end, getting through 310 people in calibration takes us three weeks. Three weeks, already, just once a year.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: So you'd say twice a year would double that.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: I'm saying it'd be hard to fit in, that's all.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Three weeks is about right. Last December it ran from the second to roughly the nineteenth, so call it seventeen days.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: There you go.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Okay, but devil's advocate, three weeks of HR time versus people feeling ignored. Which is worse?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Depends who you ask.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Which is why I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Um, I think maybe both are real, right? Like, I don't want to wave away the feedback thing.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: No, no, nobody is.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: It's just that, uh, I, I wasn't sure we had the capacity to change things.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: We don't, not this year. Paolo's team is already stretched with the payroll migration.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: That's a different question from whether it's better.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: It's a different question, but it's the one that matters for the budget.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Can we also look at lighter check-ins? Not full reviews.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Is that, um, is that something people want?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Maybe. Short. Managers just write a few lines.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: That sounds like a second review with a nicer name.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: It isn't. No ratings.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: I mean, managers should be doing that anyway in their one-on-ones.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Half of them don't, going by the pulse survey.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: That's a manager problem, not a cycle problem.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Maybe both.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. I think maybe we can park the check-ins? Because that's, that's another conversation.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm not trying to shut it down.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: It's fine.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Oh, speaking of one-on-ones, did anyone see Kaveh's note about the new scheduling thing?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Which note?

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: He sent something Tuesday, the, the shared calendar slots for managers. I think it was Tuesday. Or Monday.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Monday. Subject line says "slots."

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Right, that. Anyway, I replied but I'm not sure he read it.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: I'll ask him.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Does that have anything to do with us?

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Not really. I was just thinking of it.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Back to reviews.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Yes. Right. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: So who else is against changing? Because it feels like Chloe's the only one making a case.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: I'm leaning toward keeping it, honestly. I just wanted numbers on the table.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Elif?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Annual's fine for now.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: That's very brief.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: It's what I think.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Okay. I'll say it once more. Somebody in March has a bad month and gets a rating in December that reflects March.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Managers are supposed to account for the whole year.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Supposed to.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Recency bias, yeah. It's in the literature, I can send a link.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Um, that'd be good, Jonas. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: I'll find the paper. I read it a while ago, don't remember the author.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: I'm not saying switch. I'm saying we should know what we're giving up.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Fair.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Yeah, fair. That's, that's fair.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Is anyone going to disagree with keeping it?

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: I just did, kind of. But I'll lose.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: You, um, you're not losing, it's just - okay.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: I'm kidding, mostly.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Okay. So, uh, I think I've heard enough. We stay with the annual review in December, no second cycle this year.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Do I update the calendar hold for the calibration weeks?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Um, yes, if you could.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: I'll keep the second through the nineteenth.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Sure, that, that works.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Thandi needs an answer?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: I'll tell her this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Tell her the feedback complaint is real, though.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: I will. I will mention it.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Maybe we do something small for the newer people. Like a welcome thing at ninety days.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Now you're the one adding a cycle.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: It's not a review, it's a coffee.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: That's what they all say.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Let's, uh, let's take that offline.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Fine. Next time.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Also, the budget sheet. I need the headcount numbers from Milan by Friday.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Has he got them?

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: He says Thursday. I'll believe it Thursday.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: He's usually okay.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Usually.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: I'll nudge him too.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Anything else? I have a call at the top of the hour.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Um, no, I think that's it. Thanks everyone.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Bye.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Okay, um, I think maybe we can start? Is, uh, is Jamal back yet?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: He's in the vendor call till half past. He'll skip.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Right. Right. So the webinar this morning, did anyone, um, check how it went?

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Thirty-eight showed up out of forty-four registered. Three people signed up Wednesday night.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Thirty-eight, that's a lot better than I figured.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Last year was about thirty, so yeah.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: And the chat was busy, there was a whole thread on dependent coverage, someone asked if - well, actually it was two people, one of them was from the Leeds office, and -

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Chloe.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Sorry. Sorry. Anyway, Bao's putting the recording up on the intranet.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Okay. Can you check the date on the page this time?

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Ha, yes. I'll check. Twice.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Is the recording the whole hour?

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Forty minutes, plus the Q and A, so -

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Fifty-five with the Q and A.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Fifty-five, yes, that.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Good. Good. Um, so, the, uh - the review thing again. Elif, you said you had something before we started?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Yeah. Engagement survey cut came in this morning, split by tenure.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Okay, and, um, what does it -

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Newer people. Under two years. Forty-seven percent say they don't get feedback often enough.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: And the leavers we were sorry to lose, last eight of them, five put lack of feedback in the exit notes.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Five of eight. Um. That's - okay.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Is the eight just the regretted ones, or everyone? Because more than eight left since January.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Regretted only. Last eight.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Okay. Small number, but fine.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: I mean, I did say last week I hear this from the newer folks, but I thought it was a few loud people -

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Forty-seven percent isn't a few.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: No. No, okay.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: How big is that group, anyway?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Under two years is about a third of the company.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Closer to a hundred and ten of the 310, I'd say.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: So that's, um, that's a lot of people.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Where did we land last week? The annual?

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: December only. I kept the calibration hold, second to nineteenth.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Okay, so can I say it? I've been quiet about this for a week.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: You weren't quiet.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Fine, quiet-ish. One review a year doesn't work. By the time anyone hears about March it's December, and there's nothing they can do with it. It just lands way too late to be any use.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: But the managers are -

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Managers are supposed to cover it in one-on-ones, I know, and Jonas says half of them don't.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Pulse survey says that, yeah. About half.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: That's a manager problem though.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Then it's a manager problem sitting inside a system that gives them one formal moment a year.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Um, so -

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Hang on, let me finish. A rated one in June and another in December, people hear where they stand twice. And if somebody's slipping in the spring, we catch it in June with half a year left to fix it.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Right. Um, so -

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Sorry, I just - what do managers do in the June one, same forms?

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Don't know. Doesn't have to be the same forms.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Six hours each is the full write-up. That's the cost there.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Then make it shorter.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Then it's the check-ins again.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: With ratings.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Which I said last week -

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Not today's question.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah. The, um, the form thing, can we - later.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Yeah, but what about the three weeks? Calibration for 310 people, twice that is -

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Seventeen days last time. So thirty-odd days across the year.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Which is the whole point. When does anybody do their actual jobs?

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: June's lighter though. Nobody's closing the year in June.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Um, Paolo's team is still on the payroll migration, though. That was the capacity thing.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Till September, last I heard. End of Q3.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: So June is awkward this year. Fine. That's a timing problem, not a reason to keep a bad design.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Okay, but I worry about two sets of ratings, people getting fixated -

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Devil's advocate against myself, yes, it'll stress people out. So does a surprise in December.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: There's something in that. I found the paper, by the way. Recency bias was worse with a single yearly rating.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Oh, thanks. Can you send it round?

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Sending now. No author in the file name, sorry.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Okay, um. Let me think out loud for a sec. We said December only last week, and I, I told Thandi that.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: You did.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: So I'd have to, uh, un-tell her, which is - fine, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Better than five more regretted leavers.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah. Okay. So, uh, not December only. We're moving to two rated review cycles a year, June and December.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Oh. Okay. Just like that?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Um, does anyone want to say something against, before I -

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: No. I'd have gone the other way last week, but five of eight in the exit notes is hard to argue with.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: I'm not happy about the calibration but I can't un-hear the survey.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll stop.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Thandi?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: I'll message her after this. Tell her what changed, the survey and that.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Do I change the calendar hold, or leave it?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Leave it for now. I'll, um, work out the June side with you after.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Okay. Keeping the December one as is.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Should I draft something for the managers?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Not yet. Let me talk to Thandi first.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Elif, can I get the survey cut? I'd like to see the breakdown.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I'll send it.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Separate thing, did Milan send the headcount?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Um, not to me.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: He said Thursday. It's Thursday.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Thursday's not over.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: It's almost one.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Kaveh answered my note, by the way. The slots thing.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Oh, good, what did he say?

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: That the slots are optional for now. Or he said soft launch. I don't know what that means.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: It means optional.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Okay then.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: I need to run to another call, so -

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Same, actually.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks all.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Bye.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Um, okay, I think maybe we can, uh, start? Jamal's still out, right?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Back Monday. Or Tuesday. One of those.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Either way, not today. So, um, the offsite room, has anyone heard from Bao?

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Bao said the room's confirmed for the ninth, but the projector thing is still open, and I also wanted to ask if -

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Whose is the projector?

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Facilities. I'll chase it.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Okay, good. Um, so -

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Before we go on, did the exit interview template ever get updated?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Not yet. I think maybe next week.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Fine. I keep getting the old one in my inbox.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Right, I'll, uh, I'll look at that. Jonas, you had numbers from, um, from the June round?

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Yeah. I pulled the logs yesterday. Hang on, let me find the right tab.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: The tab with the green header?

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: No, that's the budget one. Okay, here.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: So the first June cycle. Managers logged nine hours each on average. That's from the time entries, not a survey guess.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Nine? We were all saying six.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Six was the old survey figure, the December write-up. And calibration, the thing that used to take us three weeks, ran five. It collided with the promotions work.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Five weeks.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: About that. And, um, 22 percent of managers submitted late. Roughly one in five, a bit more.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Twenty-two. Um. That's more than I figured.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Late by how much?

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Median was four days. A few were over a week.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Okay, so some of that's the June calendar. People were out.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Some, sure. I don't have the reason column filled in yet.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Right. So, uh, so the promotions overlap, was that, was that avoidable?

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Probably, if we'd put the promo window somewhere else. Nobody did.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Paolo's team asked for a freeze on the system, too.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Two days. It's in the five weeks.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Okay. Okay, so the -

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Can I say something? Because I've been sitting here doing the math and I don't love it.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Sure, um, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Two rated cycles basically doubles what we ask of everyone, managers and us both, and what do we get? I saw the pulse results this morning, feedback satisfaction went from 53 to 56. Three points.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: That's it. That's what the extra cycle bought, so I'm not sure it's earning what it costs.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Three points isn't nothing.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: It's inside the noise, Camila, it's a pulse survey.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Margin on that survey is about two and a half, three. So she's not wrong.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Okay, but it's one round. You can't judge a new thing by round one.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: I'm not judging it by round one only. The hours are real. The late submissions are real.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: The hours are partly because it's new. First time everyone's writing a mid-year form.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Or not.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Or not. Fine. But can we agree the satisfaction number takes time to move?

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Maybe. People answered that survey, what, a week after the ratings went out?

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Something like that.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: So it's measuring the immediate reaction.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Which is my point.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Or it's measuring that people got a second rating and shrugged.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Um, I, I think maybe both of those could be true.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Both can't be true.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Well, no, I mean, it could be a bit of each.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Devil's advocate, though. Nine hours versus six. If the form's shorter next June, that comes down.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: We'd have to actually shorten it. Nobody has.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: I know. That's the form conversation.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Which, um, we keep saying later.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Because it keeps being later.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Yeah, that's, that's fair.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: What about the five weeks. That's not a form problem.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: No. That's scheduling. Calibration for 310 people doesn't get faster because the form's shorter.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: It would if the promotions weren't on top of it.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: It might get back to four. Three, I doubt.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Four weeks twice a year is eight. Last year was three.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Eight, yeah, versus three. Well, plus whatever December does.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Right, so December's also, I don't know, December's three or four. So we're, what, seven or eight versus three.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Seven to eight, yeah, roughly.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: That's an if, though. We don't know December yet.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: True. December hasn't happened.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Right. Um, that's, that's the thing. We only have one data point.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: One bad data point.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Or one early one.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Same thing.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Oh, this reminds me. Thandi was asking at the all-hands, or no, it was the lunch thing, whether managers get any training before the next one, and I said, well, I said we'd see, because honestly last time they all just got an email with the forms attached, and I remember because I sent that email, and -

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Chloe, um -

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Sorry. Right. But is that something? Training?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: It might be. I'd, uh, I'd have to ask what budget there is.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: There's a small line for it. Not much.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: How small?

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Under four thousand. I'd have to check.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Okay, so a short session, not a workshop.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: It would help with the late submissions, probably.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Maybe. People who are late are usually the ones who skip the email.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Then training won't reach them.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Thank you, Elif, very cheerful.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: It's true.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Okay, um, let's, let's not solve that part today.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Fine. I just wanted it written down somewhere.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Noted. Noted.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Back to it, though. Chloe, what would you want instead? Because you're against it, but not exactly for anything.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: I don't know yet. I'm not saying throw it out. I'm saying the numbers don't justify it yet, that's all.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: That's a pretty strong all.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Maybe. I'm still thinking.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: I can break the late ones down by team, if it's useful. Might show whether it's concentrated.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Oh, that'd be, um, that'd be good.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: I'll try for Monday. Milan has the org mapping and I'm still waiting on his file.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Of course you are.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: It's been a week.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: I'll, um, I'll nudge him. Again.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: And the satisfaction number, can someone get the breakdown? Newer people versus everybody.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I can pull it. The tenure split.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: That's the one that matters. Because if the under-two-years group moved a lot and everyone else didn't, that's a different story.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Yes. Probably.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Or it moved less for them, and then I'm right twice.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Nobody's keeping score.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: I am a little.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Okay, so, um, where are we. I, I don't want to rush this.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: We aren't deciding today.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: No, no. I mean, I think maybe we need the tenure split, and Jonas's team breakdown, first.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: That's Monday, hopefully Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: So, um, nothing changes today. We pick this up next time, once those are in.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Works for me.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Okay. I'll bring my objections in a better order.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Oh, and Kaveh's slots thing, did anyone ever sign up?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I did. Once.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: I looked at it. It was a lot of boxes.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Right. Okay. I have to jump to another call, so -

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Same.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Thanks, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Bye.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Okay, um, I think maybe we can start? Is it just us today?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Jamal's still out. Everyone else is here.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Right. Right. So, uh, first thing, the offsite room. Chloe, did the projector get sorted?

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Facilities said Monday, but then I got an email from someone else saying Tuesday, and I think that was Bao's, or maybe it was -

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: So not sorted.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Not confirmed. I'll chase it again.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Okay, good. Um, and the exit interview template, I haven't forgotten, I just -

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: It's been three weeks, Mateo.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: I know. I know. I'll send it to Elif this week.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Before I forget, Milan finally sent the org mapping. Wednesday night, no message, just the file.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: It's fine, it's all there. I just had to dig through the folder to find it.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Oh good. Um, so, can we - the other thing. The review structure.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Here we go.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: So, uh, the quarterly people meeting was Tuesday. Thandi had the review item on the list, and, um, as I sat there I realized I couldn't explain why we're doing what we're doing. So I want to look at it again, properly, before I go back to her.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Look at it again meaning reopen it?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Yes. Reopen it. Both ways, nothing's settled.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: I thought we were waiting on the tenure split.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I sent it. Monday.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Oh. I haven't opened it.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Under two years moved four points. Everyone else, about one.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Four. That's not nothing.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Margin's still two and a half, three. So it's, what, barely outside the noise.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Barely outside is still outside.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: I'm only saying.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: And the late ones by team, Jonas?

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Done. It's lumpy. Mostly three teams, and two of those were mid-promotion window. The rest is scattered.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: So the late ones aren't really a design problem.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Partly. I don't have the reason column done.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Can I - sorry - can I go back a step?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Sure, um, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Because I did some reading after the people meeting, and honestly I've changed my mind a little. There's a number I keep coming back to. Managers who actually hold a one-on-one every month, their reports say they're getting enough feedback, seventy-one percent, and that's the same whether the company reviews once or twice. It barely moves with the cycle.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: So to me the fix is the monthly conversations, that's where the feedback comes from. And then the formal review can just sit at one a year, half the load, and nobody's missing out on anything.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Where's the seventy-one from?

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: The pulse survey, split by manager habit. Jonas had the cut.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: I did. Yeah, that's right. I ran it against the cycle and it was flat.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Flat how? Like, flat for both cycles?

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Seventy-one for the ones on two cycles, and seventy-one-ish for the older single-cycle data.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Hm.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: And the other group, the managers who don't do the one-on-ones, they're way down, whichever cycle.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Okay, so devil's advocate. You're saying a second rating adds nothing.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: I'm saying it adds nothing that a monthly chat doesn't already do, and it costs nine hours a manager.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: And five weeks.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: And five weeks, yes.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: But half the managers don't do the monthly chat. You said that yourself, it's a manager problem.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: It is. So we fix that. Not with a rating.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: With what? A memo?

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: With the slots thing, maybe. Kaveh's calendar -

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Um, can we hold the slots for a second? Because I, I want to hear what Camila's got.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: I think you lose the June catch. Somebody slipping in spring, we notice with half a year left.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Their manager notices. In the one-on-one.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: If they're having one.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Recency paper still says a single yearly rating is worse, for what it's worth.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Worse by how much? I only skimmed it.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: I'd have to reopen the file. It wasn't huge.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Wasn't huge.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Okay but small isn't zero.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Neither is nine hours.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: That's fair. That's actually fair.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Um, sorry, so what about Paolo's team? The payroll migration, they're still stretched, right?

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Through September. Another June-style crunch in December would hit them just after.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Right. Yeah. That's what I figured.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Also Thandi said at lunch she'd like it to be simple. Whatever we pick, she wants one page.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: She says that about everything.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: She does, but it's true.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Okay. Okay, um. Let me, let me just think for a second.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Take your time.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: It's, uh, it's mostly the load, isn't it? And the numbers on the feedback are about the same either way.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: That's how I read it.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: I still think we're giving something up.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: You, um, you might be right. But I don't think I can justify the weeks.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Fine. I said it. For the record.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: It's on the record.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Elif, can you take the December dates to the managers? The self-assessment due date and the calibration weeks, the whole calendar.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Sure. When?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: This week, ideally. Before people book leave.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Today if Jonas gives me the hold dates.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Second to the nineteenth. Same as before. I never moved it.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: So the June hold goes away?

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: I haven't touched it. I can delete it after.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Um, yeah, whenever, there's no rush on that.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Should I stop the draft for the managers? I'd started a short one.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Oh, you started one?

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: A paragraph. Just the intro.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Keep it, you can reuse it. Elif's sending the dates anyway.

utterances.speaker: Chloe
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Do you want me to loop Thandi, or you?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Me. I'll message her after this, tell her what the meeting came to.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: And the one-on-one thing, who owns that?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Um, not today. Can we, let's take that offline.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Mm. Okay.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I'll write it down.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: One more thing, headcount. Milan's numbers don't tie to the budget sheet. Off by about eleven, maybe twelve.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Eleven. Okay. I'll ask him.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Thanks. I'm not going to chase him again.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: You will.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: I have to jump to a call, so -

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Same.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Thanks, everyone.
